questions.0.explain.t: The vault hands the secret only to whoever has permission, with auditing and rotation.

questions.0.options.0.t: To centralize, control access to and rotate secrets, without leaving them in code

questions.0.options.1.t: Storing secrets in plain text, but in a more organized way

questions.0.options.2.t: Replacing IAM as the access control mechanism

questions.0.options.3.t: Improving the performance of the applications that read the secrets

questions.0.q.t: What is the purpose of a managed secrets vault?

questions.1.explain.t: A rotated secret stops being valid on its own, even if it leaked without any alarm.

questions.1.options.0.t: To limit the damage of a leak that nobody noticed

questions.1.options.1.t: Because secrets degrade and stop working over time

questions.1.options.2.t: To reduce the monthly cost of the secrets vault

questions.1.options.3.t: To avoid having to use MFA on accounts

questions.2.explain.t: If the workload has an identity, it does not even need to keep a password.

questions.2.options.0.t: Temporary credentials via the workload's identity

questions.2.options.1.t: A long random password in an environment variable

questions.2.options.2.t: A configuration file in a private repository

questions.2.options.3.t: A shared key held by the responsible team

questions.2.q.t: What is better than a static secret for a workload in the cloud?
